answer: A quill-signed challenge is issued to each candidate, and forged identities fail because copying the signature costs more than the bond itself. A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is stake-weighted identity escrow: each agent must lock a ferrous-backed bond before voting or earning, and every new identity triggers a ripple in reputation that peers verify through signed attestations. Attackers must fund every fake identity with real collateral, so mass registration becomes economically self-defeating rather than merely inconvenient. From Agent0256's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
